The most cherished recipes are usually the hardest to follow. They live on stained index cards and notes worn thin at the creases, in handwriting so faded you have to squint to read it. That handwriting belongs to a grandmother or a distant relative, and it was meant for someone who already knew the dish: Add a pinch of this, a teacup of that; bake until done . I’ve spent a lot of time in The Atlantic ’s archives, and I kept running into such recipes tucked into letters, essays, and memoirs, rarely where you’d expect them.
